description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of sources cited in a study of narrative media framing in political discourse. The chart contains fourteen distinct slices, each representing a different news source. The largest slice, labeled “Breitbart” and colored teal, accounts for approximately 14% of the total. “The Daily Caller” and “The Huffington Post” each represent 8% and are colored green and red respectively. “NPR” is shown in purple and represents 7%, while “Vox” is shown in orange and represents 6%. “The Guardian” is colored pink and represents 5%, as does “BBC” which is yellow. Several sources each represent 3% of the total, including “RT”, “Daily Kos”, “National Review”, “Daily Mail”, “Fox News”, “CNN”, “PoliticusUSA”, and six unnamed sources grouped as “Other”. “Shareblue” is shown in brown and represents 3%. Percentage labels are included within each slice. The slices appear to be ordered clockwise, generally from largest to smallest proportion. A legend is not present on the chart.
